text: Neural pull-push pyramid fill: holes of any size filled in one pass
description: More instant than an NCA, much cheaper than diffusion. Build a certainty-weighted mip pyramid (pull), then push coarse levels back into low-certainty pixels, with a tiny learned conv at each level adding detail and style. The cost is O(1) passes regardless of hole size, which makes it a natural fit for certainty weights.

status.comment: Hole-aware mip pyramid with push-pull fill + per-pixel net reading triangle taps on 5 levels (torch + net.frag, parity e6df8e5). 2026-11-23: learned downsampling in torch (net.down, a124954): per level a zero-initialised 1x1 conv over the 2x2 children (rgb, inv*near, hidden, coverage) added to the averaged hidden channels. A/B from nice-net, 500 its, same config otherwise (runs/down vs runs/nodrop; down was resumed once from its it-250 checkpoint after an earlyoom kill): 96-frame val 0.1476 vs 0.1560 (-5%); evaluate.py 64x96: all pixels net vs push-pull -14.0% vs -18.9%, holes +11.8% vs +12.1%. So: less drift over long rollouts, no gain on holes. Not in the runtime yet (needs a per-level pass instead of the C-image blits in world.rs build_mips; net.json 'down' + weights appended). Next: a longer run (2000 its) before porting.
